title: ci: fetch only exact review-base history for automated planning
body:
## Retained review checkpoint: planning repair verified; registry failures remain explicit

This focused shared-code contribution is ready for **substantive review**, not a claim of all-green registry CI or original scientific qualification. The head remains `42edc5dbcd1f7f8afa21ac76e7ee7faa1497ccb5`: two code files, with the successful automated planning job and 734-test helper result below (710 passes / 24 platform skips / zero failures or errors).

At the retained checkpoint, the existing global run had reached package replay. A bounded, non-atomic snapshot of the first 257 materialized jobs contains one successful plan plus 166 successful replay jobs, 16 failed replay jobs, four running and 70 queued. This is not completion of the 3,961 selected packages. The 16 preserved failures classify as 13 selected-result pin contradictions, two intake-record pin contradictions and one invalid SOURCES usage role. The relevant guard/input/manifest bytes are identical on canonical main `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a` and this repair head, whose diff changes only the workflow and new test module. This is source-level attribution against observed failed job logs, not an executed main baseline or proof that all later registry failures have the same cause. No frozen package, verifier, source pin or failure rule was changed to obtain green.

**Maintainer action requested:** review/adopt the two-file planning repair and decide cancellation/disposition of the already-failed global replay. The signed-in contributor account's Chrome run menu exposes no cancellation action. A complete registry pass or check waiver remains the repository maintainer's separate decision.

The exact reviewed integration for affected PR #6588 is prepared at [staging commit `311e1b1c29a401e08f7dc1be911ffc34865ffd59`](https://github.com/Clear1nsight/integer-mult-bounds/commit/311e1b1c29a401e08f7dc1be911ffc34865ffd59), sole parent `ff7df8391c3bb3f5518ce43682ba4c1e41380e3e`. It preserves the complete research subtree `a49046ef00e16dd73e6fff7144605f448aefc52a`. The actual #6588 head has not moved, and its new-head planning check remains unmet. Holding this byte-identical staging candidate until upstream adoption avoids deliberately queuing a duplicate 3,961-package replay. Staging is not another contribution PR or an original qualification.

The exact per-job evidence and public handoff are recorded in the continuation delivery comment. The original financial-meter, owner/bootstrap, compiler-input and complete control qualification remain NO-GO. All historical failures and costs remain retained.

<details>
<summary>Retained implementation, first failure, correction, validation and predecessor credit</summary>

## Change and mathematical scope

Fix the planning checkout that exhausted its unchanged 10-minute job limit on [PR #6588, run 41717679316](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41717679316). The failure occurred while checkout fetched all branches/tags/history; Python setup, helper tests and package selection never started.

Automated pull-request and main-push planning now starts with depth 2 and fetches the exact event-base commit at depth 1 only when it is missing. It validates a complete commit ID, disables replacement objects for the acquisition step, verifies the fetched commit, preserves HEAD, and stops before planning on an unavailable or invalid base. The all-zero push base retains the existing all-tracked selection.

The unchanged onboarding suite also consumes two immutable historical source snapshots. A separate pre-onboarding step obtains the exact original package commit `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90` and its source base `6f100d4bb5083f8c35d96fd95a539811c62f245c`, at depth 1 only when missing, with raw commit identity checks. Existing regression tests, historical source roles and pins are retained.

Manual dispatch retains full history and its existing revision/ref vocabulary. Replay checkout, source-history validation, package discovery, global invalidation, read-only permissions, matrix/concurrency limits and job timeouts are unchanged. This workflow change still selects every registered package under the existing global-control contract; this is not a draft exemption or a plan-only CI bypass. No mathematical result, completion of compiler-input closure or the bootstrap-control campaign, performance gain, or completed original research activity is claimed.

## Task and overlap

Originating affected delivery: [PR #6588](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6588). Related reviewed alternative: [PR #6690](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6690), which is not an adopted code dependency. The existing fixture-maintenance controls originate in [PR #4984](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4984).

Explicit assignment: repair the checkout failure and finish the submission audit. Scope is unchanged. Base: `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a` (canonical main, refreshed before publication). The patch contains only the owning workflow and one regression-test module.

- [ToikY's #6690](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6690), inspected at `aba156a1131a99ef054fd2f4407ac5718a4959c0`, archives a proposed blob-filter patch for both full-history checkouts. It remains a review-only alternative: its production workflows do not apply that proposal. This change instead narrows automated planning history while preserving replay history.
- [Tekalign's #3142](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3142) and [Arham-Tahir64's #3102](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3102) establish sparse declaration/reference handling. Their adopted discovery behavior is reused unchanged.
- [Clear1nsight's #4984](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4984) supplies the fixture maintenance controls used here.
- [#6588](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6588) is the affected research-archive consumer. This focused shared-code PR keeps its repair separately reviewable.

The overlap search covered current and closed/merged PRs, relevant code/function names and the existing canonical handoff; it is a bounded search, not a novelty claim.

## Validation

The initial 17-case candidate was executed once on a read-only five-file cold copy containing the exact candidate workflow/tests and unchanged pinned selector, batch workflow and publication-history checker. Repository-root reproduction form:

```sh
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_plan_checkout.py' -v
```

The actual local invocation used `/usr/bin/python3 -B -m unittest discover -s <pinned-read-only-cold-copy>/tests -p test_research_plan_checkout.py -v`, with the cold test directory supplied as an absolute path. It did not execute from a full repository checkout.

Initial local result: **17 tests passed, zero failures/errors/skips**, 3.598 seconds reported by unittest (3.662 seconds subprocess wall observation), local Linux/Python 3.12. The source/test/command were independently reviewed before the parent executed them; all five post-run hashes match the reviewed bytes. This is AI-assisted independent source/oracle review, not human review or a proof-kernel result.

The tests execute the actual extracted workflow Bash step in local file-transport Git repositories. They cover an older multi-commit push base missing from depth 2; a synthetic PR merge compared to the exact event base in shallow and full repositories; available bases with a dead remote; 40/64-zero bases; malformed/missing/injected bases; missing commits, blob IDs and failed fetches; replacement-ref controls; unchanged HEAD; failure before a selector-entry sentinel with existing output preserved; no unrelated tags/branches; manual relative/tag/remote refs; static assertions preserving the source-history shallow/ancestry guards; and unchanged global invalidation for both shared workflows. Fixture Git commands disable automatic maintenance/GC. The original source-history runtime fixtures remain part of hosted helper compatibility verification; the new static method does not execute those fixtures.

The new acquisition step assumes the existing fresh Ubuntu Actions checkout, immediately after the pinned checkout action. It is not a standalone Git API for arbitrary inherited repository/configuration redirections. The existing selector's Git environment sanitization remains intact.

Local tests do **not** establish GitHub network checkout time or the full repository helper glob. The actual PR must demonstrate checkout, `Onboarding helper tests` and exact-base selection completing within the unchanged 10-minute planning job. Registered replay will retain its actual pending/pass/fail/skipped state; planning success alone is not full CI or scientific acceptance. No manual historical replay or timing reroll was performed.

Initial candidate SHA-256: workflow `8252d171742499cdef8ffd28d7ab9da4f4be0c57845f0eea14a6f32c84278b52`; tests `abe6db0db44bb66ce527e5f519c55a7df88cbb462fc07b6c10592d6ede037aee`.

### Preserved first hosted result and correction

[Run 41727490575](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41727490575), attempt 1, at initial head `9283c240a3e9b085bc89e0e5b8f407dae4e24463`: checkout passed in 168 seconds and exact-base acquisition passed. The full helper glob ran **728 tests in 152.923 seconds, with 10 errors and 24 platform skips**. All 10 errors came from `test_research_descendant_source_roles.py` trying to read the absent historical package commit. Selection and replay were skipped. The failed run is preserved; it was not rerun unchanged.

The correction restores the specific historical snapshot dependencies before the unchanged helper suite. It does not replace them with current bytes, skip the tests, edit their oracle, or substitute full-history assurance with a shallow replay. Corrected-source local and hosted outcomes will be recorded in the delivery note against their exact head; the initial 17-case pass is not transferred to the correction.

Six additional controls extend the regression module to 23 cases: two genuinely missing historical snapshots with original blob availability despite changed HEAD; an already-complete inventory with a dead remote; a partial inventory followed by fetch failure before an onboarding-entry sentinel; invalid/zero/empty/unavailable inventory; raw replacement-ref refusal; and a drift assertion deriving the declared inventory from the actual existing test's ORIGINAL constant and current SOURCES.base_commit. A source audit separately checks all six historical path/blob/SHA-256 rows and the four transitive code bodies. The two-commit inventory qualifies this existing dependency; future history consumers require an explicit inventory/contract review.

## Credit

Prepared for Clear1nsight with substantial OpenAI Codex / GPT-6.1-sol assistance, including separate source/oracle review. Retain Douglas Colkitt and Charles Bethin's shared planner/selector credit, Tekalign and Arham-Tahir64's sparse handling, and the predecessors linked above. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Verify this exact PR's automated checkout, full helper glob and selection in hosted Actions; retain the original failed run. If checkout still exhausts the cap, diagnose its exact phase before choosing another acquisition strategy.
2. After substantive upstream review/adoption, apply the repaired workflow to the affected #6588 delivery and verify that actual head. Until then its old failed run remains failed.
3. Replay retains full history because its source-history contract is stronger. Its checkout cost is a separate boundary; any future change needs that contract and controls rather than inheriting this plan-only history change.

Original financial-meter/owner/bootstrap and compiler-input/control qualification remain unresolved. This infrastructure repair adds no original activity credit and does not resume a closed research round.

</details>
